doc.title: Chico Hamilton — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Recording Topsy before Cozy Cole
summary: Hamilton says he was first to record Topsy with a small group before Cozy Cole had a hit with it.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: You talk about the fraternity of drummers and, you know, when we look at it through the historical perspective we know that Papa Jo -- you know, when you came to New York you had to come to Papa Jo’s house, you know, and there seemed to be a real fraternity and real nurturing. You know, we know that drummers as you’re the first to admit, you know, kind of out to lunch to be drummers and sometimes there’s some competition, you know, people, you know, got their turf, but then there seemed to have been a history or a legacy, more of a fraternal -­
Oh, yeah, for instance I’m the first one to record Topsy with a small group, right. Cozy Cole recorded Topsy and made a zillion dollars, it became a hit, right.
When did you record Topsy because -­
As a matter of fact, he heard me playing it and he -­
That’s the biggest selling drum solo record ever.
Yeah, right. He heard me playing it. He didn’t know anything about Topsy.
But he was doing (unintelligible) solos. That was his thing back in the day.
